label: rigiditytheorem
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{rigiditytheorem}
Let $(S_1,h_1)$ and $(S_2,h_2)$ be marked, closed, oriented Riemannian surfaces of genus $g$, and of curvature strictly less than $-1$. There exists a $(2,1)$-dimensional marked $GHCC$ anti-de Sitter spacetime $X$ into which $(S_1,h_1)$ and $(S_2,h_2)$ embed respectively as the past and future boundaries. Furthermore $X$ is unique up to isometries preserving the marking.

title: Lemma and Definition
body_md:
\label{lemma:ExistenceAndUniquenessOfAutomorphicFieldsI}
Let $\rho:\Pi\rightarrow\mathrm{P}\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ be Fuchsian. For every cocycle $\alpha$, there exists a unique continuous $(\rho,\alpha)$-automorphic vector field $\xi_\alpha$, which we call the \emph{automorphic vector field} of $\alpha$. This vector field is of Zygmund type. In particular, it is of H\"older type $C^{0,\eta}$ for all $\eta<1$.

title: Proof
body_md: Since the set of points of $\mathrm{P}\mathbb{R}^1$ which are attractive fixed points of $\rho(\gamma)$ for some non-trivial $\gamma\in\Pi$ is dense in $\mathrm{P}\mathbb{R}^1$, uniqueness follows from \eqref{eqn:FormulaForAutomorphicVectorField}. Existence is proven, for example, in \cite{GL}. Likewise, by \cite[Section 16.6]{GL}, $\xi_\alpha$ is of Zygmund type, and this completes the proof.

For every $\rho$-cocycle $\alpha$, there exists a unique continuous $(\rho,\alpha)$-automorphic vector field $\xi_\alpha$, which we call the \emph{automorphic vector field} of $\alpha$. The restriction of this vector field to $\Lambda$ is of Zygmund type. In particular, it is of H\"older type $C^{0,\eta}$ for all $\eta<1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since every $(\rho,\alpha)$-automorphic vector field takes the form $\xi:=(\xi_r,\xi_l)$, existence and uniqueness follow by Lemma \ref{lemma:ExistenceAndUniquenessOfAutomorphicFieldsI}. To prove the Zygmund property note that, since $\Lambda$ is the graph of a homeomorphism $\phi:\mathrm{P}\mathbb{R}^1\rightarrow\mathrm{P}\mathbb{R}^1$, in particular, it is rectifiable, and each of the two projections $\pi_r,\pi_l:\Lambda\rightarrow\mathrm{P}\mathbb{R}^1$ restricts to a Lipschitz function over $\Lambda$. It follows by Lemma \ref{lemma:ExistenceAndUniquenessOfAutomorphicFieldsI} that $\xi=(\xi_r\circ\pi_r,\xi_l\circ\pi_l)$ is of Zygmund type, and this completes the proof.

\label{lemma:LocationOfFurthestPoint}
There exists a compact subset $K$ of $\Sigma$ and $\epsilon>0$ such that, for all $p\in\Sigma\setminus K$, the furthest point of $\zeta_p$ from $\zeta_0$ is an element of $\zeta_p([-\pi/2+\epsilon,-\epsilon])$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(p_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a divergent sequence in $\Sigma$. For all sufficiently large $m$, let $t_m\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ be such that $\zeta_{p_m}(t_m)$ is the furthest point in $\zeta_{p_m}$ from $\zeta_0$, and suppose that $(t_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges to some limit $t_\infty$, say. It will suffice to show that $t_\infty$ is an element of the open subinterval $]-\pi/2,0[$.

Let $\Sigma_0$ be a fundamental domain of $\Sigma$ and, for all $m$, let $\gamma_m\in\Pi$ be such that $\widetilde{p}_m:=\rho(\gamma_m)\cdot p_m$ is an element of $\Sigma_0$. We may suppose that $(\widetilde{p}_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges to some limit $\widetilde{p}_\infty$, say. For all $m$, denote $\zeta_m:=\rho(\gamma_m)\cdot\zeta_0$ and $\widetilde{\zeta}_m:=\rho(\gamma_m)\circ\zeta_{p_m}$, and note that $(\widetilde{\zeta}_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges to $\widetilde{\zeta}_\infty:=\zeta_{\widetilde{p}_\infty}$. For all $m$, let $\eta_m$ denote the unit speed parametrized spacelike geodesic in $\mathrm{AdS}^{2,1}$ joining the furthest points of $\widetilde{\zeta}_m$ and $\zeta_m$ such that $\eta_m$ points towards $\zeta_m$, and $\eta_m(0)\in\widetilde{\zeta}_m$. In particular, for all $m$, $\eta_m(0)=\widetilde{\zeta}_m(t_m)$ and $\partial_s\eta_m(0)$ is orthogonal to $\widetilde{\zeta}_m$ at this point. For all $m$, let $\eta_m(\infty)$ denote the end-point of $\eta_m$ in $\partial_\infty\mathrm{AdS}^{2,1}$.

Recall now the full translation map $\tau$ defined in Section \ref{sss:AntideSitterSpaceInMatrixModel}. Since $(\tau(\zeta_m))_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ diverges in $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{H}^2$, we may suppose that it converges to some point $q$, say, of the limit set $\Lambda$. On the other hand $(\tau(\widetilde{\zeta}_m))_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges to $\tau(\widetilde\zeta_\infty)$, which is a finite point of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{H}^2$. It follows by the ``H''-Lemma (Lemma \ref{lemma:HLemma}) that $(\eta_m(\infty))_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ also converges to $q$. The sequence $(t_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ therefore converges to a point of $\pi^{\mathrm{cyl}}_{\widetilde{p}_\infty}(\Lambda)$, and the result now follows by Lemma \ref{lemma:ProjectionOntoGeodesicOfLambda}.

label: lemma:LocalGuageEquivalence
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:LocalGuageEquivalence}
Let $\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ be a smooth, strongly convex immersed surface, and let $\pi^e:\mathbb{R}^3\rightarrow\mathrm{T}\Sigma$ denote the Euclidian orthogonal projection. If $\xi:\Sigma\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^3$ is a Euclidian first order isometric variation of $\Sigma$, then $\pi^e\circ\xi$ is everywhere locally gauge equivalent to a holomorphic function.

That is, for all $p\in\Sigma$, there exists a neighbourhood $\Omega$ of $p$, a quasiconformal homeomorphism $\phi:\mathbb{D}\rightarrow\Omega$, and a continuous orientation preserving trivialization $\psi:\mathrm{T}\Omega\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ such that the composition $\big(\psi\circ\pi^e\circ\xi\circ\phi\big)$ is holomorphic.

In particular, if $\pi^e\circ\xi$ is non-vanishing, then every zero is isolated and has positive integer-valued winding number

Moreover, it follows from \cite[Prop. 1.8]{BS3} that this set is compact. However we know from \cite{BHa} that a compact, real analytic space admits a fundamental homology class modulo $2$. label: lm:trapping
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lm:trapping}
Let $Y\in\mathcal{Y} $ be non-Fuchsian, let $K<-1$, and set
$$\Delta(K) \,:=\, \arctan\!\sqrt{|K|-1}~,$$
so that $\Delta(K)\to 0$ as $K\to -1$. Let $\widetilde S\subset\mathbb{A}d\mathbb{S}^3$ be the image under a developing map of the universal cover of $S_K^+$, and let $P$ be a support plane of the corresponding convex hull along the lift of $\partial_+C(N)$. Then the time distance from any point of $\widetilde S\cap I^+(P)$ to $P$ is at most $\Delta(K)$, where $I^+(P)$ is the future of $P$. The analogous statement holds for $S_K^-$, reversing the time orientation.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $P$ is a support plane of the convex hull, both its dual points lie on the boundary of the domain of dependence. Hence the equidistant surfaces $P_t$, $t\in(0,\pi/2)$, of $P$ foliate the intersection of $I^+(P)$ with the domain of dependence, and the time distance $u:=d(\cdot,P)$ is a smooth function there, with values in $(0,\pi/2)$ and level sets $(P_t)_{t\in(0,\pi/2)}$.

Suppose $\widetilde S\cap I^+(P)\neq\emptyset$. The restriction of $u$ to $\widetilde S$ extends continuously by $0$ to the boundary at infinity of $\widetilde S$, which is the limit set $\Lambda$; indeed $\Lambda$ is contained in the closure of the past side of $P$, since $P$ is a support plane.
Hence $u|_{\widetilde S}$ attains a maximum $t_1>0$ at an interior point $x_1$. Near $x_1$, the surface $\widetilde S$ is contained in the past of the umbilic surface $P_{t_1}$, sharing a common tangent with this surface at $x_1$, with the same future unit normal. By the comparison principle for spacelike surfaces at an interior tangency, the shape operators (with respect to the future unit normal) satisfy $B_{\widetilde S}(x_1)\leq -\tan(t_1)\,\mathrm{Id}$; since both eigenvalues of $B_{\widetilde S}(x_1)$ are then at most $-\tan(t_1)<0$, \eqref{eq:detB} yields
\begin{equation*}
|K|-1 \,=\, \det B_{\widetilde S}(x_1) \,\geq\, \tan^2(t_1)~,
\end{equation*}
that is, $t_1\leq \Delta(K)$, as claimed.

title: Proof
body_md:
The two leaves $S_K^-$ and $S_K^+$ bound a compact collar containing the convex core, which is a GHCC anti-de Sitter $(2,1)$-spacetime of genus $g$ denoted by $X_K(Y)$: the boundary components are smooth, spacelike, and strongly convex in the direction of the interior of $X_K(Y)$ by \eqref{eq:detB}, since the leaves are convex towards the convex core. By construction, $\mathcal{J}(X_K(Y)) = \left(\mathrm{I\!I\!I}_K^-(Y),\mathrm{I\!I\!I}_K^+(Y)\right)$.

\emph{Injectivity.} Suppose $\Psi_K(Y)=\Psi_K(Y')$. Since $u_{K^*}$ is injective, $\mathcal{J}(X_K(Y))=\mathcal{J}(X_K(Y'))$, hence $X_K(Y)=X_K(Y')$ by Corollary \ref{cr:III}. A GHCC anti-de Sitter $(2,1)$-spacetime $X$ admits a unique GHMC extension (see \cite{Mes}), and since $Y$ is a GHMC extension of $X_K(Y)$, and $Y'$ of $X_K(Y')$, we conclude that $Y=Y'$ as elements of $\mathcal{Y}$.

\emph{Continuity.} It suffices to prove that $Y\mapsto \mathrm{I\!I\!I}_K^\pm(Y)$ is continuous, which follows from the continuous dependence of the leaves $S_K^\pm$ on the structure. The latter is a consequence of the uniqueness part of \cite{BBZ} together with a compactness argument: given $Y_i\to Y$, the leaves $S_K^\pm(Y_i)$ are trapped in a fixed compact collar around the convex core by Lemma \ref{lm:trapping}, and have uniformly bounded geometry; any $C^\infty$-limit of a subsequence is a closed spacelike surface of constant curvature $K$ in the appropriate component for $Y$, hence equals $S_K^\pm(Y)$ by uniqueness, so the whole sequence converges.
                                                                    
                                                               

\emph{Openness.} Both $\mathcal{Y} \cong\mathcal{T} \times\mathcal{T} $ and $\mathcal{ML} \times\mathcal{ML} $ are topological manifolds of the same dimension $12g-12$ (recall that $\mathcal{ML} $ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{6g-6}$). Being continuous and injective, $\Psi_K$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset by invariance of domain.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(l_-,l_+)\in\mathcal{FML} $ and let $F:=\psi^{-1}(l_-,l_+)$. Note that $F$ contains no Fuchsian structure, since the bending laminations of a Fuchsian structure vanish, while $l_\pm$ together fill $S$.

Under the Mess identification $\mathcal{Y} \cong\mathcal{T} \times\mathcal{T} $, the map $\psi$ is the map $\Phi$ of \cite[Def.~1.7]{BS3}; it is continuous, and it is proper by \cite[Prop.~1.8]{BS3}. In particular $F$ is compact.
                                                                      
                                                   

Choose a finite family of closed curves $c_1,\dots,c_p$ on $S$ such that $l\mapsto (i(c_1,l),\dots,i(c_p,l))$ is a topological embedding of $\mathcal{ML} $ into $\mathbb{R}^p$, and equip $\mathcal{ML} \times\mathcal{ML} $ with the corresponding distance
$$ D\!\left((l_-,l_+),(l'_-,l'_+)\right) \,=\, \sum_{j=1}^p \left| i(c_j,l_-)-i(c_j,l'_-)\right| + \left| i(c_j,l_+)-i(c_j,l'_+)\right|~, $$
as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 4.9]{DS}. Let $(K_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be any sequence with $K_n\to-1$, $K_n<-1$. By Lemma \ref{lm:convergence}, for each $j$ and each sign, $L_{\mathrm{I\!I\!I}^\pm_{K_n}(\cdot)}(c_j)\to i(l_\pm(\cdot),c_j)$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathcal{Y} $; by \cite[Lemma 4.3]{DS} recalled above (applied with $T=\mathcal{Y} $ and $\kappa_n=K_n^*\to-\infty$), it follows that
$$ i\!\left( u_{K_n^*}\!\left(\mathrm{I\!I\!I}^\pm_{K_n}(\cdot)\right), c_j\right) \;\to\; i\!\left(l_\pm(\cdot),c_j\right) $$
uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathcal{Y} $. In other words, $\Psi_{K_n}\to\psi$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathcal{Y} $ for the distance $D$.

By Lemma \ref{lm:embedding}, each $\Psi_{K_n}$ is an embedding of the manifold $\mathcal{Y} $ into the manifold $\mathcal{ML} \times\mathcal{ML} $. By Finney's theorem (\cite[Thm~1]{Fin}, see \cite[Thm~4.6]{DS} for the form used here), the compact fiber $F$ is therefore a cellular subset of $\mathcal{Y} $.

Finally, by Lemma \ref{lm:analytic}, $F$ is a compact real-analytic subset of $\mathcal{Y} $, hence an absolute neighborhood retract by Sullivan's local description of real-analytic sets \cite{Sul} and Hanner's criterion \cite{Han}, see \cite[Lemma 4.8]{DS}. A cellular subset which is an ANR is contractible, see \cite[Lemma 4.7]{DS}. Therefore $F$ is contractible.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cr:landslide}
  For all $\theta_-,\theta_+\in(0,\pi)$ and all $h_-,h_+\in\mathcal{T} $, the composition
  $$\mathcal S_{e^{i\theta_+},h_+}\circ\mathcal S_{e^{i\theta_-},h_-}:\mathcal{T} \longrightarrow\mathcal{T} $$
  has a unique fixed point.

title: Proof
body_md: Let $K_\pm=-1/\cos^2(\theta_\pm/2)\in(-\infty,-1)$. By the dictionary between the landslide flow and constant curvature surfaces in GHMC anti-de Sitter $(2,1)$-spacetimes (\cite[Lemma 1.9 and Corollary~4.2]{cyclic}, and the translation carried out in \cite[Section 9]{cyclic2}), the fixed points of $\mathcal S_{e^{i\theta_+},h_+}\circ\mathcal S_{e^{i\theta_-},h_-}$ are in bijection with the GHMC anti-de Sitter $(2,1)$-spacetimes $Y$ for which the constant curvature $K_-$ (resp. $K_+$) surface in the past (resp. future) of the convex core has induced metric homothetic to $h_-$ (resp.\ $h_+$). It is therefore enough to show that there is exactly one such $Y$. However this is a direct application of Theorem \ref{rigiditytheorem}, when restricted to metrics of constant curvature.
